Use the questionnaire number as a reference.

Questionnaire schedules target a questionnaire to specific employees across one or more legal entities. Schedules are typically created in the GCO entity and can be released to individual schools or across all companies. Open the Questionnaire module From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Modules ▸ Questionnaire ▸ Distribute ▸ Questionnaire schedules. Create a new schedule Click Questionnaire schedules in the left menu, then click New. Select the questionnaire In the Questionnaire field, select the questionnaire to distribute. The questionnaire must already exist in the system before it can be scheduled. Set up the questionnaire details Click Setup details in the Action Pane. Select the person, teams or business segments to specify which school or group of schools the questionnaire is released to. Set the date range Enter a Start date and End date for the questionnaire window. Respondents will only see the questionnaire within this active period. Start the schedule Click Start to activate the schedule. The questionnaire will appear for targeted employees in the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal under their Questionnaires tab.

As your retention conversation with an employee progresses, update their status in the Intentions Inquiry to keep the record up to date. Open the intentions inquiry Navigate to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Inquiries and Reports ▸ Employee Intention Survey Result and locate the employee. Edit the record Click Edit to put the record into edit mode. Most fields are read-only. Only the Retention Status and Comments fields are editable. Update the retention status Select the appropriate status from the Retention Status dropdown: Status When to use HR Discussion A retention conversation has been initiated Retained successfully The employee has agreed to remain Exit confirmed The employee is confirmed as leaving — triggers the recruitment process Add a comment Enter any relevant notes in the Comments field to document the outcome of conversations or actions taken. Save Click Save to record the change.

The Employee Intention Survey Result form displays all employees who answered "Yes" to the intention-to-leave question in the Intention Questionnaire. Responses are captured live as employees submit the survey through Employee Self-Service (ESS). Navigate to the intentions inquiry From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Inquiries and Reports ▸ Employee Intention Survey Result. Review the list The form displays all flagged employees. Columns include: name, search name, school, school code, business segment, position, job, email, intention to leave response, and retention status. The list is pre-loaded with historical data and receives new live submissions as employees complete the questionnaire. You can build filters to segment employees by retention status stage or school. Open a record Click on an employee's record to open the full detail view, including their questionnaire response and current Retention Status.

Request types define what employees can request through the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal, which fields appear on the submission form, what is required before submitting, and which approval workflow the request follows. Open the Human Resources (HR) request types form In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the HR request types form within the Human Resources module: Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ HR request types. Select a request type Choose the request type to configure — for example, Police Clearance Certificate, Early Exit, or Home Location Change. Configure the fields Click Header setup. For each field on the request type, set: Toggle What it does Visible Shows the field on the employee's ESS submission form Mandatory Requires the employee to complete this field before submitting The Attachment option is present on every request type by default — employees can always attach a file, so it does not appear in the field list. Assign a workflow Return to the main request page. Select the approval Workflow to apply to this request type from the dropdown. If multiple workflows exist, choose the appropriate one for this type (for example, routing to the WSO HRBP approval group). Control ESS visibility Toggle WebESS display to show or hide this request type in the employee portal. Request types that HR initiates internally should be set not to display in ESS. Set the display order Enter a value in the ESS display order field. Lower numbers appear first in the ESS request list (e.g., 1 = first). Assign a high number to push a request type to the bottom of the list. Save Click Save to apply the configuration.

When an employee submits a request through Employee Self-Service (ESS), it is routed to the Human Resources (HR) team via the configured workflow. HR reviews the submission, provides feedback, and marks it complete. Open the HR Request form In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the HR Request form within the Human Resources module. Click Refresh to load any new submissions. Each submitted request has a system-generated request number. Open the request Click on a request to open its detail view. You can see: The employee's submitted field values (e.g., destination, date, reason) Any file the employee attached, which you can open or download Review the submission Read through the employee's details and verify the request before taking action. Enter HR Feedback In the HR notes field, enter your response or notes. This text is visible to the employee when they view their completed request in ESS. Attach a document (optional) If you need to provide the employee with a document — such as an approval letter — click Attach to upload a file. The employee will be able to download it from their request in ESS. Approve and complete the request Click Approve to approve the request, then click Complete to mark it as done and close the workflow. Note: After completing a request there is typically a 3–5 minute delay before the updated status appears in ESS. The ESS cache refreshes on a 5-minute cycle — this is by design.

When an employee's recorded times are wrong—the biometric machine wasn't working, or they raised an Human Resources (HR) request for a late arrival or early exit—you correct the attendance log and re-run the summary. Use this route for a one-off correction; for bulk corrections, load them through the import instead. Open the attendance logs In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log. Find the record Filter to the employee and the date you are correcting. Apply the filter before you edit so you don't accidentally change anyone else's record. Edit the times Click Edit and change the Clock in date time to the correct values. Make sure the Code remark in column matches the correct action. Save Click Save. Re-run the summary batch job Go to Time and attendance ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Execute attendance summary and click OK. Wait for the message centre to confirm completion. This step is not optional. The attendance log is the raw record; this job calculates the work duration, regular minutes, and overtime everyone uses. Until it runs again, your correction exists only in the log. Check the corrected record in D365 Go back to Time and attendance ▸ Attendance details, or to Employees ▸ Work ▸ Attendance ▸ View attendance on the employee, and confirm the corrected times and the recalculated duration. Check it in Employee Self-Service (ESS) Open the employee's attendance in ESS and check the same date. ESS refreshes with a five-minute delay rather than instantly, so allow a moment before deciding the change hasn't taken effect. The interval is deliberate—the attendance feed arrives once a day, so refreshing the portal221 every minute would cost performance for no gain.

An employee's attendance and overtime are visible to, and approved by, whoever sits above them in the attendance and overtime hierarchies. You set that on the employee's position. Until you do, only the line manager sees them. Open the employee In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Positions ▸ All positions and open the employee whose approver you are setting. Open their position Open the employee record and open the Reports to position tab. You will see the line manager already recorded. Add the attendance and overtime hierarchy Open the Relationships tab. Click + Add to assign the person or position that will approve the employee's attendance and overtime. This is often the same person as the attendance approver, but it doesn't have to be. Save Click Save. The employee now appears under that approver when they switch to the hierarchy view in the attendance details and overtime details forms in D365, and under Hierarchy on the team attendance screens in Employee Self-Service (ESS). Where the line manager is also the attendance and overtime approver, you can leave these unset — the employee will appear under the line view instead. An employee who is in neither your line nor your hierarchy does not appear for you at all, by design.
documents.s: Assign attendance and overtime managers to a position

documents.t: Three people approve overtime in sequence: the manager first, then Human Resources (HR), then finance. Each stage sees only what the previous stage approved, so the list gets shorter as it moves along. Open the HR approval form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the HR approval form. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ HR approval. Review what has reached you Only the records the manager has already approved appear here. If a manager approved three records, you'll see the same three— everything else they left is not on your list. The Last modified by and date and time columns show who approved the record before you and when. Approve as HR Select the records HR is approving and approve them. You do not have to approve everything that reaches you — approving two of three records sends only those two on. Save Click Save. Open the finance approval form Go to the Finance approval form. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Finance approval. Approve as finance The records HR approved are the ones listed here. Review the date, time, and punch location for each, then approve. Overtime that has cleared all three stages is what gets sent out for payroll processing. At the time this was recorded, the payroll integration was still being built with the Phoenix team, so check with your system administrator what the current hand-off to payroll is.
documents.s: Complete the HR and finance overtime approvals

documents.t: Two parameter settings drive the whole time and attendance process: the hierarchies that decide who approves attendance and overtime, and the threshold below which overtime is not worth raising. Set both before you load any attendance data. Open the human resource parameters In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Human resources parameters and open the General tab. Set the attendance and overtime hierarchies In the hierarchy area, you will find two fields — one for Attendance and one for Overtime. Select the position hierarchy you want each to use. These exist because the person who approves attendance is not always the line manager. If a separate designated employee handles attendance or overtime, the hierarchy you select here routes it, and you assign individuals to that hierarchy based on their position. If the line manager approves attendance and overtime, you can point both fields to the line hierarchy—there is no problem with that. Save the parameters Click Save. Set the minimum overtime threshold Go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Human resources shared parameters and enter the minimum number of minutes to treat as overtime. Anything below the value you enter here will not show up as overtime. This keeps trivial daily overruns—five minutes past the end of a shift, for example—out of the overtime forms so approvers see only overtime that matters. Save the shared parameters Click Save. The threshold applies from the next run of the attendance summary batch job. Next, put people into those hierarchies — see Assign attendance and overtime managers to a position.

If you need attendance logs for employees with no punch data—because they aren't on the biometric system or a period needs backfilling—you can have Dynamics 365 (D365) generate them from a default start and end time and a working time calendar. It creates one punch in and one punch out for each applicable working day in the range. Open the attendance logs form In D365, go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log. Open the generation form Click Generate attendance log in the Action Pane. Set the punch in details Enter the Start date time—the date the range begins and the time to use as the punch in (for example, 10 August at 07:00) —and set the Code remark in to Punch in. Set the punch out details Enter the End date time using the punch out time (for example, 17:00), and set its Code remark out to Punch out. The start and end date and time define the punch in and punch out times used on every generated record. Set the generate-to date Enter the Create till date — for example, 14 August. This is how far forward the records are generated. Select the working time calendar Choose the working time calendar to apply. It determines which days in the range count as working days, so non-working days produce no records. Select the workers Under the workers area, narrow to the employees you want. Available criteria include position, tier, department, staff category, and staff level, or you can select named employees from the list. Generate Click Generate attendance log. A notification confirms how many employees were processed. Check the generated records Refresh the attendance logs form and filter to the personnel numbers and the entry dates you generated. You should see a punch in and a punch out for each applicable working day in the range, with the code remarks you set. The process is safe to re-run over the same period. Re-running with the same parameters does not create duplicates — existing records are left unchanged, and only records that are missing, for example, a day someone has deleted, are generated again. Generated records feed the normal process from here. Run the attendance summary batch job over them as you would over imported punch data — see Run the attendance summary batch job.

Attendance data reaches Dynamics 365 (D365) as punch records — a clock-in and a clock-out per employee per day. An integration with the biometric system delivers these automatically, so you won't run this import daily or weekly. Use it when the integration isn't in place yet, or to correct or add records in bulk. The Excel or comma-separated values (CSV) import below is how the data gets in. Open a data import project In D365, go to System administration ▸ Workspaces ▸ Data management and click Import. Name the project Give the project a Group name. If you are duplicating an existing project, give it a different name so you don't overwrite the original. Select the entity and file type Set the file type to CSV and select the Time and attendance entity. Upload the file Click Upload and select your file, then apply it to the project. Map the remaining columns You may see a warning that the entity is not fully mapped. Map any outstanding fields — the code remark, the timestamp, the device ID and the device location — then apply the mapping. Run the import Click Import now. The file loads into the attendance log table. Check the loaded records Go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log and review what came in. Each row holds the entry date, employee ID, clock-in date and time, code remark in, any remark passed through from the time and attendance clock, the clock-out date and time, and the location and device it was recorded on. Work duration is not calculated at this point. The attendance log is only the raw record of a punch-in and punch-out—durations, regular minutes, and overtime are calculated by the summary batch job. To run the summary, see Run the attendance summary batch job.

Overtime details is the manager's view of overtime in Dynamics 365 (D365), and the first of the three approval stages. It is the same approval the manager can do from Employee Self-Service (ESS) — whichever route is used, the record is the same. Open the overtime details form In D365, go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ OverTime detail. Understand what you are seeing Only employees with overtime records appear here. The form includes a filter option in the overtime minutes column to view employees with logged overtime, so it is a working list rather than a full roster. Overtime below the threshold set in the human resource shared parameters is excluded too — see Configure time and attendance parameters. Narrow to a date range Set a From date and To date and click Get data to see overtime between those dates. Switch between the line and hierarchy views As with attendance details, Line shows your direct reports and Hierarchy shows the people assigned to you through the overtime hierarchy in your position. Check who last changed the record The Modified by and Modified date and time columns show who last touched each overtime record, so you can see whether an entry has been amended and by whom before you approve it. Approve Click Edit, then select the records you want to approve. You can select one record, or several for the same employee, and approve them together. Click Approve. The Total approved minutes updates as you approve records. Approving here is the manager stage. The record then has to pass Human Resources (HR) and finance before it reaches payroll — see Complete the HR and finance overtime approvals. An overtime record approved by the manager in ESS appears here as soon as it is approved — the two screens show the same data, not a copy. See Approve your team's overtime in the ESS guide.

The attendance details form is the summarised view of who worked what, one record per employee per day. The summary batch job builds it from the attendance logs, so anything you see here reflects the last time the job ran. Open the attendance details form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance detail. Read a record Each row shows the date, clock-in and clock-out times, work duration in minutes, regular minutes, overtime minutes, and the location, location ID, and device name the punch came from. Switch between the line and hierarchy views The form shows the employees who report to you, and you can view them in two ways. Line shows your direct reports. Hierarchy shows the people who report to you for attendance through the attendance hierarchy of their position. These are usually different sets of people, and that is the point of the two views — a designated attendance manager sees their attendance reports under Hierarchy even though those people report to somebody else on the Line. Search for a specific employee Filter on the Name column to find one person. If the employee doesn't appear, they aren't in your line or attendance hierarchy—that is a deliberate restriction, not a data problem. View one employee's own record To look at a single employee's attendance from their record instead, go to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Employees, open the employee, and under the Work tab in the Action Pane, go to Attendance ▸ View attendance. This shows all their attendance and overtime information—work duration, regular minutes, and overtime minutes—in one place, and it's the view an employee sees for themselves.

An employee who punches in in the morning but never punches out in the evening leaves an incomplete day. The missing attendance form collects these so you can chase and correct them, rather than quietly producing an incorrect duration. Open the missing attendance form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the Missing attendance form under time and attendance. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Missing attendance. Read the exceptions Each row is a day when one half of the pair is missing: a punch in with no punch out, or a punch out with no punch in. Both cases are recorded as missing attendance. Switch between the line and hierarchy views As on the other attendance forms, Line shows your direct reports and Hierarchy shows the people assigned to you through the attendance hierarchy. Correct the record Once you have established what the missing time should have been — from the employee, their manager, or an Human Resources (HR) request for a late arrival or early exit — correct it in the attendance logs and re-run the summary batch job. See Adjust an attendance record.

Attendance logs contain only raw punch records. The Execute attendance summary job reads them and creates the summary record for each employee and day—their work duration, regular minutes, and overtime minutes—which every other attendance screen and the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal read from. In normal operation, this runs as a recurring batch process right after the data feed, so nobody runs it by hand. Run it manually when you have just imported, generated or adjusted attendance logs and want the results now. Open the job In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Execute attendance summary. You can also search for Execute attendance summary in the search bar. Run it Click OK. Wait for the message centre to confirm The message centre tells you when the run is complete. Check the results Go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance detail and find an employee in the batch. Each day's record shows the clock-in and clock-out times, work duration, regular minutes, and any overtime minutes. For example, an employee who clocked in at 08:00 and out at 17:05 shows a work duration of 545 minutes, 480 regular minutes, and 65 minutes of overtime. Their location, location ID and device name carry through from the imported log. Run this job again any time you change an attendance log. Editing the log on its own changes nothing downstream — see Adjust an attendance record.
documents.s: Run the attendance summary batch job

documents.t: Overtime eligibility is decided by staff level, not person by person. Flag the categories that can claim overtime once, and every hire into a position in one of those categories picks up the flag automatically as their worker action completes. Open the staff levels form In Dynamics 365 (D365), open the Staff levels form (Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ Staff levels) and find the staff position category and staff category you are setting — for example, transport support and support staff. Tick the overtime flag Set Overtime applicable against that category. Only staff in categories flagged here are treated as eligible for overtime. Unflagged categories produce no overtime records, no matter how many extra minutes their attendance logs show. Save Click Save. The setting takes effect for worker actions completed from now on — it does not retrospectively update people already hired. Complete the hire worker action as usual Hire the employee through the normal worker action process, with a position whose staff position category and staff level match the one you flagged. Submit the action to workflow and let it be approved. The worker action has to be completed, not just submitted. The flag is written to the employment record during action processing, so it isn't there while the workflow is still running. Check the flag on the employee Once the employee record has been created, open it and go to the Employment history area. Eligible for overtime is set to Yes. Amend the flag where it doesn't fit Click Edit and change the flag on the individual employee where the staff level rule isn't right for them, then Save. The staff level sets the default; the employee record records exceptions.
documents.s: Set overtime eligibility on staff levels

documents.t: Common problems in Dynamics 365 Human Resources (HR) and how to resolve them. Use the contents list on the right to jump to a section, or press Ctrl+F to search this page.

Cause — A personal or non-GEMS Microsoft account is being used, or the portal link is wrong. Fix — Sign in with your GEMS Microsoft 365 email address. The portal URL is provided by your system administrator. Where single sign-on is in use and you are already signed into Microsoft on the device, you are signed in automatically.
documents.s: I can't sign in to D365 HR

documents.t: Cause — Module visibility depends on the security roles attached to your account. Fix — Use the search bar at the top of the screen to search for the form by name. If it still doesn't appear, contact your system administrator to confirm your role.
documents.s: The Human Resources module isn't in the module list

documents.t: Cause — The pane has been collapsed. Fix — Click the hamburger menu (☰) at the top-left of the screen to expand it again. The Home icon in the pane returns you to your home page at any time.

Cause — The record is not in edit mode. Most Dynamics 365 (D365) forms open read-only. Fix — Click Edit in the Action Pane, make your changes, then click Save. The Back, Save/Edit, and New buttons stay anchored at the top of the record as you move between tabs.

Cause — A questionnaire must already exist in the system before it can be scheduled. Fix — Create the questionnaire first, then return to Questionnaire ▸ Distribute ▸ Questionnaire schedules and select it.
documents.s: The questionnaire I want isn't in the Questionnaire field

documents.t: Cause — The schedule hasn't been started, the current date sits outside the schedule window, or the recipients weren't set. Fix — Open the schedule and check three things: that Setup details names the right people, teams or business segments; that today's date falls between the Start date and End date; and that Start has been clicked to activate the schedule.
documents.s: Employees can't see the questionnaire in ESS

documents.t: Cause — Recipients are chosen in Setup details by person, team or business segment. Schedules are normally created in the GCO entity and can be released to one school or across all companies. Fix — Reopen Setup details on the schedule and correct the selected teams or business segments.
documents.s: The questionnaire went to the wrong schools

documents.t: Cause — The Employee Intention Survey Result form only lists employees who answered Yes to the intention-to-leave question. Fix — Check whether the employee has submitted the Intention Questionnaire at all. Responses appear live as employees submit through Employee Self-Service (ESS).
documents.s: An employee isn't showing on the intentions inquiry

documents.t: Cause — Most fields on the Employee Intention Survey Result form are read-only by design. Fix — Click Edit in the Action Pane. Only Retention Status and Comments can be changed.
documents.s: I can't edit the fields on an intentions record

documents.t: Cause — The exit survey is generated by a batch job that only picks up employees who have been assigned an offboarding checklist. Fix — Confirm the employee has an active offboarding checklist, then run Questionnaire ▸ Periodic Question ▸ Questionnaire Schedule for Offboarding Employee. The batch can also be scheduled to run nightly.
documents.s: The offboarding exit survey hasn't been issued

documents.t: Cause — Answers are held separately from the schedule record. Fix — Go to Questionnaire ▸ View and analyse results ▸ Answers by person, filter to the employee, then click Answers in the Action Pane. Use the questionnaire number as your reference.
documents.s: I can't find an employee's questionnaire answers

documents.t: Cause — Either no default checklist is nominated in HR parameters, or the action type used for the hire doesn't have the checklist flag enabled. Fix — Check both: Human Resources parameters ▸ Recruitment must name an Onboarding checklist, and the relevant entry in Personal action types must have Apply onboarding checklist enabled.
documents.s: No onboarding checklist was applied when the hire completed

documents.t: Cause — Checklist tasks route to the group's primary member, not to everyone in the group. Fix — This is expected. To change who receives tasks, right-click the group, choose View Details, select the correct member, and click Make Primary.
documents.s: Only one member of the group received the task

documents.t: Cause — The primary group member has an active delegation configured. Fix — Delegated tasks route automatically to the delegate. Check the primary member's delegation settings if this wasn't intended.
documents.s: The task went to someone outside the group

documents.t: Cause — The task has a dependency on another task that hasn't been finished. Fix — The task detail view in ESS shows which tasks are blocking progress and who is responsible for them. The task unlocks once all dependencies are complete.
documents.s: An employee can't complete a task in ESS

documents.t: Cause — The task's Company field is either set to the wrong legal entity or left blank. Tasks with no company set apply to all schools. Fix — Open the task in the checklist and set Company to the specific legal entities the task should apply to.
documents.s: A task is appearing for the wrong school

documents.t: Cause — User groups are scoped by legal entity. Employees at other schools aren't visible in the current context. Fix — Switch legal entity context to the relevant school, or use the position, job title and name filters to narrow the visible list.
documents.s: I can't see the employees I want when building a user group

documents.t: Cause — Onboarding and pre-onboarding checklists calculate dates differently. Fix — Onboarding tasks use due date offset from start date — days after the employee starts. Pre-onboarding tasks use an offset date — days before the target date set when the checklist is applied. Check which type of checklist you're editing.
documents.s: The task due dates are wrong

documents.t: Cause — The Process type in the checklist assignment dialog is set to Pre-onboarding. Fix — This is expected — only checklists matching the selected process type are listed. The onboarding checklist is applied automatically once the worker action is fully approved and completed.
documents.s: Only pre-onboarding checklists are available on the worker action

documents.t: Cause — Dropdown values come from the Visa master setup tables, which were pre-loaded during migration. Fix — Add the missing value under Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master — Visa Type, MOL Profession, MOE Profession, or Contract Type as appropriate — then click Save.
documents.s: A visa type or profession is missing from the dropdown

documents.t: Cause — Codes on their own are ambiguous. Fix — Descriptions are displayed alongside codes in every dropdown selection. If a description is missing, add it to the profession record in the Visa master setup.
documents.s: I can't tell the profession codes apart in a dropdown

documents.t: Cause — Alerts are driven by the saved expiry date and the threshold configured for that document type. Fix — Confirm the expiry date is recorded on the visa or identification record. Thresholds — how far ahead the alert triggers — are configured per document type in system setup, so a passport alert may start 50 days out while another type starts closer to expiry.
documents.s: No expiry alerts are appearing for an employee's documents

documents.t: Cause — No documents currently fall within the configured expiry threshold. Fix — No action needed. Open Human Resources ▸ Workspaces ▸ Personnel management to see the tiles for each document type.
documents.s: The Expiring Records tile is empty

documents.t: Cause — ABC Category is derived from the visa type. Fix — Change the Visa Type on the worker action and the ABC Category updates automatically.
documents.s: The ABC Category field won't let me change it

documents.t: Cause — Identification records carry over to the Pending Worker Visa Information form, but only publish to the employee record when the worker action is completed. Fix — Open Pending Worker Visa Information, find the worker, and click View Documents to confirm the records are present. Then complete the worker action through the standard workflow. Afterwards, verify in Employee Visa Information and in the employee's Person Identifications.
documents.s: The applicant's passport details didn't carry over to the new employee

documents.t: Cause — The form only holds pending worker actions that are not yet complete. Fix — If the worker action has already been completed, look at the employee record instead. If the hire hasn't been initiated, start the worker action first.
documents.s: A worker isn't listed on the Pending Worker Visa Information form

documents.t: Cause — The WebESS display toggle is switched off for that request type. Fix — Open the request type in Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ HR request types and switch WebESS display on. Request types that HR initiates internally are deliberately hidden from ESS.
documents.s: A request type isn't showing in ESS

documents.t: Cause — The list is ordered by the ESS display order value. Fix — Set a lower number to move a request type towards the top of the list, and a high number to push it to the bottom.
documents.s: Request types are in the wrong order in ESS

documents.t: Cause — The field is set to Visible but not Mandatory. Fix — Open Header setup on the request type and switch the Mandatory toggle on for that field. Employees then can't submit until it's completed.
documents.s: Employees are submitting requests without the information we need

documents.t: Cause — Attachments are available on every request type by default, so the option isn't listed as a configurable field. Fix — No action needed. Employees can always attach a file to any request.
documents.s: The Attachment option isn't in the field list

documents.t: Cause — No approval workflow has been assigned to the request type. Fix — Open the request type, select the appropriate Workflow from the dropdown, and save.
documents.s: A submitted request isn't going to anyone for approval

documents.t: Cause — The list holds its loaded state. Fix — Click Refresh on the HR Request form to pull in new submissions. Each has a system-generated request number.
documents.s: New submissions aren't appearing on the HR Request form

documents.t: Cause — The ESS cache refreshes on a five-minute cycle. Fix — Allow 3–5 minutes for the updated status to appear. This delay is by design.
documents.s: The status still shows as pending in ESS after I completed the request

documents.t: Cause — The response was recorded somewhere other than the field ESS surfaces. Fix — Enter your response in the HR notes field. That text is what the employee sees on their completed request. Any file you add with Attach is downloadable by the employee from the same place.
documents.s: The employee says they can't see our response

documents.t: Cause — One of several things stops the batch creating a review: the review date falls outside the horizon, the date has already passed, the employee is excluded, or the batch hasn't run. Fix — Check in order — that Exclude from Probation is set to No on the employee record; that the Stage 1 or Stage 2 date falls within the Probation Horizon Days value; and that Generate probation review has run under System Administration ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Batch. Reviews are not generated retrospectively for dates that have already passed.
documents.s: No probation review was generated for an employee

documents.t: Cause — Probation parameters are set per combination of Staff Level and Default category, and the employee's combination may be configured differently — or may not match the one you expect. Fix — Check the employee's staff level and category, then review that row's Stage 1 and Stage 2 review days and template in the probation configuration form.
documents.s: The probation dates or template are wrong for an employee

documents.t: Cause — Reviews are routed into the manager's queue by the batch, not created directly on the employee record. Fix — The review appears in the manager's ESS queue under Team Probation Review Requests once the batch has run and the Review 1 Generated or Final Review Generated flag is set to Yes.
documents.s: The manager can't find the review

documents.t: Cause — Probation status is not updated automatically. Fix — After a Stage 2 review completes with a Meets Expectations outcome, HR is notified. Open the employee record, go to Work history, and set Probation Status to Confirmed.
documents.s: An employee has passed probation but their status still isn't Confirmed

documents.t: Cause — Where the outcome is Performance Concerns, the workflow routes to HR only. Fix — This is by design — the employee is not notified. HR takes the appropriate next steps directly.
documents.s: The employee wasn't told their Stage 2 outcome

documents.t: Cause — The review record shows the current status, not the full routing history. Fix — Open the review in HR Probation Reviews and click View History to trace each action, which workflow conditions evaluated true or false, and when each step completed.
documents.s: I need to see who actioned each step of a review

documents.t: Cause — An attachment is mandatory for that document type at that company, and no file has been uploaded. Fix — Upload the supporting file and the Submit button becomes available. To change the rule, update Attachment mandatory for company on the identification type.
documents.s: The Submit button is disabled in ESS when adding an identification document

documents.t: Cause — Mandatory fields are configured separately for each identification type. Fix — This is expected. A passport asks for issue date, end date and place of issue; Khamra asks for an agency rather than a country; medical insurance requires no issuing agency.
documents.s: Different document types are asking for different fields

documents.t: Cause — Rules are scoped by legal entity (company) and by Worker region. Fix — Open the identification type and check both scoping settings so the requirement only applies to the intended schools or locations.
documents.s: An identification rule is applying to the wrong staff

documents.t: Cause — Components with no Reward Type set are excluded from the statement. Fix — Open the component in Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Compensation ▸ Component master, click Edit, set a Reward Type, and save.
documents.s: A component isn't showing on the employee rewards statement

documents.t: Cause — The Reward Type value determines which category the component appears under. Fix — Change the Reward Type to the correct option — Fixed Allowance, Living, or Other — and save.
documents.s: A component is showing in the wrong category

documents.t: Cause — The component master lists every component regardless of configuration. Fix — Filter the Reward Type column to where the value is not empty. That shows everything currently included in the rewards statement; clear the filter to find components still to be configured.
documents.s: I can't tell which components have already been configured

documents.t: Cause — The checklist must exist and have a primary task owner before it can be assigned. Fix — Go to Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Offboarding checklists, select or create the checklist, assign the monitoring group under Assigned to, select a user and click Make Primary, then save.
documents.s: I can't assign an offboarding checklist

documents.t: Cause — The Process type in the Apply checklist dialog is set to something other than Offboarding. Fix — In Actions ▸ Checklists ▸ Apply checklist, set Process type to Offboarding, choose the checklist, and click OK.
documents.s: The offboarding checklist isn't available on the employee's action

documents.t: Cause — Task dates are calculated from the target date set when the checklist is applied. Fix — Set the Target date to match the termination end date entered on the personnel action. Individual task dates are then derived from each task's offset.
documents.s: The offboarding task due dates look wrong

documents.t: Cause — Nothing has been received from GEMSU for that employee, or the message failed to import. Fix — Open the GEMSU integration log for the employee. If there is no entry, confirm with the GEMSU team that the course was assigned at source. If there is an entry in an error state, raise it with the GEMSU team — the message arrived but couldn't be written to the course tables.
documents.s: An employee's GEMSU courses aren't showing on their record

documents.t: Cause — The status update hasn't come through from GEMSU yet. Fix — Check the integration log for a more recent message against that employee. If the latest message imported successfully and still shows the old status, the source record in GEMSU hasn't been updated.
documents.s: The employee says the course is complete but D365 shows it in progress

documents.t: Cause — GEMSU course records are written by the integration and are not maintained by hand in D365. Fix — Correct the record in GEMSU and let it flow through, or load the correction through the GEMSU course data entity.
documents.s: I can't edit a course record on the employee's tracker

documents.t: Cause — The tracker on the employee record is scoped to that employee. Fix — Use the all-employee GEMSU course form and filter by course status or course type — for example, to list everyone with an outstanding mandatory course.
documents.s: I need to see course status across the workforce, not one employee at a time

documents.t: Cause — The most common reason is an employee ID in the file that doesn't match a personnel number in D365. Fix — Review the failed rows reported against the import project, correct the employee IDs and any field mapping, then re-run just the failures.
documents.s: My Excel import of course data failed

documents.t: Cause — The integration carries current course data; it does not backfill history. Fix — Load the historical records through the GEMSU course data entity. See Import GEMSU course data manually.
documents.s: Historical course data from before go-live is missing

documents.t: Cause — Either the plan is hidden at header level, the leave type is restricted, or the employee isn't enrolled. Fix — Check the ESS visibility flag on the leave plan header, then the restriction on the individual leave type — either one hides the type on its own. If both are set correctly, check the employee's enrolment under Leave and absence on their record.
documents.s: An employee can't see a leave plan in ESS

documents.t: Cause — The dropdown follows the sort order set on each leave type. Fix — Set the sort order on the leave types so the most commonly requested appear first.
documents.s: Leave types appear in the wrong order in ESS

documents.t: Cause — The hire action ran without the leave plan flag, or no plans are configured against their staff level. Fix — Check that the personnel action type has Update leave and absence plan set to Yes, and that the staff level for that position has leave plans assigned for the legal entity. Enabling the flag afterwards does not retrospectively enrol the employee — the enrolment has to be corrected separately.
documents.s: A new starter has no leave plans

documents.t: Cause — A promotion adds the new staff level's plans alongside the existing enrolment; the old ones go when the previous position is retired. Fix — Retire the previous position if that is your process. Retiring the position also retires the plans attached to it.
documents.s: A promoted employee kept their old leave plans

documents.t: Cause — The workflow has no condition on the system generated leave flag. Fix — Open the Leave and absence request workflow for that legal entity and add the condition that auto-approves requests where system generated leave is Yes.
documents.s: Calendar-change requests are sitting in review instead of auto-approving

documents.t: Cause — Balances recalculate when the system-generated request completes, not at the moment the holiday is moved. Fix — Wait for the adjustment requests to reach completed, then check the balance again as of a date after the change.
documents.s: I moved a holiday but the balance hasn't changed

documents.t: Cause — The filters were cleared or select all was used on an unfiltered list. Fix — The requests are created and approved immediately, so they have to be cancelled individually. Filter by position type, department or staff category and confirm the selection before clicking Assign leave.
documents.s: Bulk leave requests were created for the wrong staff

documents.t: Cause — They are still within probation, where a certificate is required from the first day. Fix — Check their probation status on their work history. The threshold on the leave type only applies once the employee is Confirmed.
documents.s: An employee is being asked for a medical certificate on a short absence

documents.t: Cause — The leave falls outside the cancellation window, which is measured from the leave start date. Fix — Cancel it in D365 on their behalf, or adjust the parameter if the window is consistently too short for your schools.
documents.s: An employee can't cancel leave they need reversed

documents.t: Cause — The most common reason is that no fare record matches the employee. The calculation needs a record in the airfare setup for their legal entity, their route, their ticket class and their ticket type, covering the dates the batch was run for. Fix — Check the air ticket location from and to fields on the employee's profile against the From city and To city on the fare records for their company. If those match, confirm the employee has a confirmed worker benefit enrolment — eligibility is derived from it, and employees without one are skipped.
documents.s: No airfare was calculated for an employee

documents.t: Cause — The active dependent flag is not set to Yes, the dependent has no valid from date, or the number of active dependents exceeds the entitlement on the benefit enrolment. Fix — Open Personal contacts on the employee record and check the active dependent flag first — dependents without it are skipped entirely. Then check the valid from and valid to dates, and the entitlement on the enrolment: self + 3 covers three dependents, and a fourth is not calculated.
documents.s: A dependent has no calculated line

documents.t: Cause — The entitlement doesn't cover the whole airfare period, so the fare has been reduced by days. Fix — This is expected. The calculation is the full fare divided by the days in the year and multiplied by the days covered — counted from the employee's employment start date, or from the dependent's valid from date. See Review calculated airfare.
documents.s: The amount is less than the full fare

documents.t: Cause — Their birth date means they crossed an age group boundary during the period. Fix — This is expected. The days before the birthday are paid at the lower fare and the days after at the next one, and the line carries the combined amount. Check the bands in Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Age group setup if the split doesn't look right.
documents.s: A dependent was paid at two different fares

documents.t: Cause — The calculation runs from the dependent's valid from date, which is the date the record became valid rather than the date of birth. Employees often add a dependent weeks after the birth, once the paperwork is through. Fix — Correct the valid from date on the personal contact, delete the employee's existing calculated lines, and run the batch again for that employee.

Cause — A duplicate check blocks a second record for the same legal entity, the same from and to city, and the same dates. Fix — Find the existing record for that combination and amend it, or delete it before creating the replacement. The same check applies to rows loaded through the data entity.
documents.s: I can't save a new fare record

documents.t: Cause — Records are being created by hand. Fix — Use the data entity instead. On the Airfare setup form, click Open in Microsoft Office in the Action Pane and select the airfare data entity. The year's rates can be loaded across every legal entity in a single upload. See Set up airfare rates.
documents.s: The whole year's fares need loading and there are too many to key in

documents.t: Cause — The batch writes new lines; it doesn't overwrite the existing ones. Fix — Delete the employee's existing lines on the calculated airfare form first, then run the batch again for that employee and the same period.
documents.s: I corrected the data but the amounts haven't changed

documents.t: Cause — The daily rate is the fare divided by 365 regardless of how long the period actually is. In a 366-day period the days covered are counted for real but still divided by 365, so the last day or two of cover makes no difference to the amount. Fix — This is how the calculation is specified. A full-period entitlement takes the full fare directly, so it is never overpaid; only part-period lines in a leap-year period round up like this.
documents.s: An employee covered for almost the whole of a leap year got the full fare

documents.t: Cause — The from date and to date used when running the batch don't match the period on the fare records. Fix — The pro-rata is measured against the dates entered on the batch, so a mismatch skews every line. Rerun with the dates set to the airfare period held in the airfare setup.
documents.s: The calculated amounts don't reconcile with the fare table

documents.t: Cause — The creation date falls outside the performance period selected. Fix — The creation date must sit inside the start and end dates of the period you are releasing. Check it against the period dates and run the job again. See Generate performance reviews.
documents.s: The performance review batch ran but no reviews were created

documents.t: Cause — It is being searched for by name rather than opened from where the custom jobs are grouped. Fix — Go to System administration ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ GEMS periodic batch jobs. Probation, performance and talent review jobs are all grouped there.
documents.s: I can't find the performance review batch job

documents.t: Cause — The personnel number was left blank. Fix — This is how the job works: a blank personnel number generates for everyone in the legal entity. Enter a personnel number to generate for one employee only.
documents.s: The batch generated reviews for the whole company

documents.t: Cause — The review template selected doesn't match the period being released. Fix — Each period has its own template. Check which template is attached to the run and reissue with the matching one. The goals on a review are copied from the template at the point of generation, so correcting the template afterwards doesn't update reviews already created.
documents.s: Reviews were generated but carry the wrong goals

documents.t: Cause — No goal templates have been added to the review template. Fix — Open the review template and add the goal templates it should carry. See Set up review templates.
documents.s: A generated review has no goals on it

documents.t: Cause — The scores are calculated when the manager submits the end of year review. Fix — This is expected before submission. If the scores are still zero after the end of year review has been submitted, check that the rating weight factor is switched on for the review template — without it the calculation doesn't run.
documents.s: The total and average scores are showing as zero

documents.t: Cause — The performance year is not attached to the period. Fix — Open the period and set the Performance year. Every period needs its year attached. See Set up performance periods.

Cause — None are recorded against them by design. Fix — This is expected. performance improvement plan (PIP) and personal development plan (PDP) goals are released ad hoc to support an employee's development and sit outside the weighted scoring.
documents.s: PIP and PDP goals have no ratings or weightings

documents.t: Cause — Managers comment at goal setting but do not rate. Fix — This is expected. Ratings start at the mid year review.
documents.s: The goal setting reviews have no manager ratings

documents.t: Cause — No calibration framework has been set up against the performance year. Fix — Open the performance year, open its calibration framework, and enter the expected percentage for each rating band. See Set up the performance year and calibration framework.
documents.s: Calibration has nothing to compare against

documents.t: Cause — The employee has not been calibrated yet. Fix — This is expected until HR calibrates them. Filtering on blank calibrated ratings gives you the outstanding list. See Monitor the calibration inquiry.
documents.s: The calibrated rating is blank in the calibration inquiry

documents.t: Cause — The manager has not published to their direct reports yet. Fix — Release to manager and publish to employees are two separate steps. Check the released to direct reports flag in the calibration inquiry to find the managers who still have a step outstanding.
documents.s: Ratings were released to the manager but the employees still can't see them

documents.t: Cause — A value can only be defined once across the growth and performance matrix. Fix — Clear the value from its existing box before placing it in the new one.
documents.s: I can't place the same measure in two boxes on the matrix

documents.t: Cause — The update isn't instant. Fix — Allow a moment and refresh. The placement is written to the employee's talent review record under the Work tab. See View talent review records.
documents.s: A matrix move in ESS hasn't appeared on the employee record

documents.t: Cause — The attendance log holds the raw punch records only. Durations, regular minutes and overtime are calculated by the summary batch job. Fix — Run Time and attendance ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ SQ attendance summary. In normal operation this is a recurring batch, so check with your administrator whether the schedule has stopped. See Run the attendance summary batch job.
documents.s: An employee's attendance shows no work duration or overtime

documents.t: Cause — Editing the log alone does not recalculate anything downstream. Fix — Re-run SQ attendance summary after saving the correction, then check the attendance details. See Adjust an attendance record.
documents.s: I corrected an attendance log but nothing changed

documents.t: Cause — The forms only show people in your line or your attendance or overtime hierarchy. This is a deliberate restriction. Fix — Toggle between the Line and Hierarchy views. If they appear in neither, they are not assigned to you — check the hierarchies on their position. See Assign attendance and overtime managers to a position.
documents.s: An employee doesn't appear in attendance details or overtime details

documents.t: Cause — Either their staff level isn't flagged as overtime applicable, or the overtime falls below the minimum threshold. Fix — Check Overtime applicable on their staff level and Eligible for overtime on their employment record, then check the minimum overtime value in Human resource shared parameters. Anything below that value is excluded by design.
documents.s: Overtime records aren't showing for an employee who worked extra hours

documents.t: Cause — A filter on the overtime minutes column excludes everyone with no overtime. Fix — This is expected. The form is a working list of employees with overtime, not a full roster.
documents.s: The overtime details form looks like it's missing most employees

documents.t: Cause — Only records the manager has already approved reach HR. Fix — Check whether the manager has approved in ESS or in the overtime details form. Overtime moves manager ▸ HR ▸ finance, and each stage only sees what the stage before approved. See Complete the HR and finance overtime approvals.
Cause — HR's approval wasn't saved. Fix — Reopen the HR approval form, approve the records, and click Save before moving to finance.
documents.s: Finance approval doesn't show records HR approved

documents.t: Cause — One half of the pair is missing from the feed. Fix — The day is listed on the Missing attendance form. Establish the correct time and amend the attendance log, then re-run the summary job. See Review missing attendance.
documents.s: An employee has a punch in but no punch out

documents.t: Cause — Assumed, but not the case. Fix — Re-running over the same period with the same parameters does not create duplicates. Existing records are left unchanged and only missing days are regenerated. See Generate attendance logs.
documents.s: Re-running Generate attendance logs will duplicate my data

documents.t: Cause — Some columns in the file aren't mapped to entity fields. Fix — Map the outstanding fields — the code remark in and out, the timestamp, and the device ID and device name — then apply the mapping and import. See Import attendance data.
documents.s: The attendance import warns that the entity isn't mapped

documents.t: Cause — Either the staff level wasn't flagged when the worker action completed, or the position's staff category doesn't match a flagged one. Fix — The flag is written as the hire worker action completes, so flagging the staff level afterwards doesn't backfill it. Amend Eligible for overtime on the employee's employment record directly. See Set overtime eligibility on staff levels.
documents.s: A newly hired employee has Eligible for overtime set to No

documents.t: Cause — ESS refreshes on an interval rather than instantly. Fix — Allow about five minutes and refresh. The interval is deliberate — the attendance feed arrives once a day, so a shorter refresh would cost performance for no benefit.
documents.s: A change made in D365 isn't showing in ESS

documents.t: Contract types define the employment contract categories used when recording visa and employment information (for example: Full Time, Limited, Part Time). These values are configured once during initial setup and rarely change. Navigate to Contract Type From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa Master ▸ Contract Type. The configured contract types are displayed. Add a new type Click New, complete the required fields, then click Save.

MOE (Ministry of Education) professions define the occupational classifications relevant to the education sector, used to categorise employee roles in line with Ministry requirements. Navigate to MOE Profession From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa Master ▸ MOE Profession. The full list of configured professions is displayed. Add a new profession Click New, complete the required fields, then click Save. Export the list Click Export to Excel to download the list if needed.

MOL (Ministry of Labour) professions define the occupational classifications required for labour regulatory compliance. All standard MOL professions are pre-loaded into the system. Navigate to MOL Profession From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master ▸ MOL Profession. The full list of MOL professions is displayed, including profession codes and descriptions. Descriptions are shown alongside codes in all dropdown selections to ensure clarity. Add a new profession Click New, enter the profession code and description, then click Save. Export the list Click Export to Excel to download the list if needed.

When an applicant is hired through the recruitment process, any identification records added to the applicant record (such as passport or visa details) automatically carry over to the Pending Worker Visa Information form. The Human Resources (HR) or Public Relations Officer (PRO) team uses this form to confirm documents are present and to complete additional visa-related fields before finalising the hire. Once the worker completes the action, the system publishes all information to the employee's record. Open Pending Worker Visa Information In Dynamics 365 (D365), search for and open the Pending Worker Visa Information form. Or you can access it through Human resources ▸ Workers ▸ Action ▸ Pending Worker Visa Information. Locate the worker record Find and open the record for the worker you are hiring. Records on this form correspond to pending worker actions that are not yet complete. Confirm identification documents Click View Documents in the Action Pane to view the identification records (such as a passport or visa) entered at the applicant stage. Confirm that the expected records are present. Attachments uploaded to the applicant record are also visible here. Open the worker action Click on the Action number to open the corresponding worker action form. Complete visa fields Click Edit and record the following fields as applicable. Default values configured in system setup will pre-populate where they apply: MOL Profession — Ministry of Labour classification MOE Profession — Ministry of Education classification (where applicable) Visa Issuing Unit — the issuing authority (for example, WSO) Visa Labour Card Status — select the status that applies to this worker Visa Type — select the visa category (for example, Employment Visa A). The ABC Category field updates automatically based on the selected visa type. Save Click Save to record the visa information on the worker action. Complete the worker action Return to the worker action and complete it through the standard workflow (submit for approval and approve as required). Completing the worker action converts the pending worker to a confirmed employee record. Verify the employee record Once the worker action is completed, confirm that the information has been published correctly: Open the Employee Visa Information form and search for the new employee — visa fields and identification records should be present. Open the employee's record in the Human Resources module and navigate to Person Identifications to confirm identification documents (for example, passport, visa) are listed.

The Expiring Records workspace gives Human Resources (HR) and Public Relations Officer (PRO) teams a centralised view of all employee documents approaching or past their expiry dates. Open Personnel Management Follow the pathway Human resources ▸ Workspaces ▸ Personnel management. Click the tile Click the tile to open the full workspace view. Each record shows: The employee's name and unique identifier (UID) The document type and expiry date The number of days remaining Expiry thresholds — how far in advance an alert is triggered — are configured per document type in the system setup. For example, a passport alert may begin 50 days before expiry, displaying 49 days remaining. Take action Review the list and contact or follow up with the relevant employees. Once a renewal has been processed, update the record in Dynamics 365 (D365) accordingly.

The visa information form captures all fields required for visa processing and regulatory compliance for an individual employee. This is typically completed by the Human Resources (HR) or Public Relations Officer (PRO) team. Navigate to the Employee Visa Information section. Follow the pathway: Human resources ▸ Workers ▸ Employee Visa information. Select a record Click New to start a new visa entry. View the completed fields Dropdown lists show profession descriptions alongside codes for clarity: UID Number Visa Type Visa Programme MOL Profession MOE Profession Working Unit Labour Card details ABC Category Contract Type Note: Once saved, expiry dates are monitored by the system. Alerts appear in the employee's Employee Self-Service (ESS) dashboard tiles and in the notification bell as the expiry approaches, based on the threshold configured for each document type.
documents.s: View visa information for an employee

documents.t: Visa statuses define the lifecycle stages used to track the progress of visa and labour card applications. Set these values during initial configuration; they apply to all employee visa records. Navigate to Visa/Labour card status From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master ▸ Visa/Labour card status. Review the configured statuses The list shows all available statuses. The default statuses are: Status Description Applied Application has been submitted to the relevant authority Not Applied Application has not been submitted to the relevant authority Visa Holder Visa holder LC Holder Labour card holder Edit a status To modify an existing status, click Edit on the relevant row and make your changes. Export the list Click Export to Excel to download the full list if needed. Save Click Save when complete.

Use this table to determine what visa type is valid for an employee. For example, an employee with a visit visa cannot have a work visa status. Navigate to Visa Status/Type Combination In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master ▸Visa Status/Type Combination. View the table A table outlining the Visa/Labour card status, Visa Type, and ABC code will display automatically.

Visa types define the categories of visas available when recording employee visa information. These values were pre-loaded from the organisation's prior system during migration. Navigate to Visa Type From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master ▸ Visa Type. The full list of configured visa types is displayed. Add a new visa type Click New, complete the required fields (type label and description), then click Save. Export the list Click Export to Excel to download the list if needed.

Welcome to the Learner Experience (LXP) help centre. LXP is the student-facing platform for learning, assignments, and school activities. Help articles are coming soon. In the meantime, contact your school's admin team for support.

Welcome to the Parent Experience (PXP) help centre. PXP is the parent-facing platform for notices, attendance, communication, and school updates. Help articles are coming soon. In the meantime, contact your school's admin team for support.

Use this feature to view your child's absences as a percentage. Select Absentee Percentage Click the Attendance tile on the home screen. Select Absentee Percentage from the prompts. Select the child whose record you wish to view. The absentee percentage will automatically display.

If your child will arrive late to school or will be picked up early, you can submit an attendance notice through the app to inform staff and teachers. Click Attendance Notice In the Attendance tile, click the Attendance Notice prompt. Select the relevant child and submit the notice form If more than one child is enrolled in the school, select the relevant child. Click Submit late/early notice and complete the form. Click the arrow in the top right to send the form. Note: The arrow to send the form only becomes active when all the fields are completed. Note: You will receive a confirmation message when you successfully submit the form.

Use this feature to view how many days of absence your child has. You can set the time frame to a week, term, or academic year, and include the previous academic year for comparison. Select Days Absent from the list of prompts Select the Attendance tile from the home screen. Select the Days Absent prompt. Identify the child whose records you wish to see The app will display a list of your children; select the child you want to view. Use the dropdown menu to choose the timeframe you want to view absences for.

If someone other than the registered parents/guardian is picking up your child, use the Pick-up Change form to inform the school. Select Someone Else to Collect My Child Click Attendance from the home screen tiles. Then select Someone Else to Collect My Child from the suggested prompts. Select the child and complete the pickup change form If more than one child is enrolled at the school, a list will appear. Select the child in question. Click on and fill in the Request pickup change form. Send to the school by clicking on the arrow in the top-right corner.
documents.s: Someone Else to Collect My Child

documents.t: For unexpected absences, you can submit a form to notify the school. Select the Unexpected Absence prompt Go to the Attendance tile on the home screen. Select the Unexpected Absence prompt. Select the child and complete the leave request form Select the child that will be absent. Complete the Open leave request form. Optionally, upload any supporting documents for the required absence. Click the arrow in the top right to submit the form. Note: The arrow to send the form only becomes active when all the fields are completed.

Use this page to search for the cost of upcoming activities your child is interested in enrolling in. Select Activity Cost from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Activity Cost from the suggested prompts. Follow the prompts to prepare an enquiry in the app about activity costs. The app will automatically send your enquiry to the relevant parties.

Use this page to search for dates and times of the activities your child is enrolled in. Select Activity Day and Time from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Activity Day and Time from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load.

Use this page to volunteer your time and support for a particular activity or event. Select Becoming activity volunteer from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Becoming activity volunteer from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load. Select the event you would like to volunteer for. Follow the prompts to sign up.

Use this to cancel or withdraw your child from an activity or event they are already registered for. Select Cancel event/activity registration from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Cancel event/activity registration from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load. Select the activity you wish to cancel registration for or withdraw from.

Use this page to search for the member of staff heading a particular event or activity. Select Contact Person for an Activity from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Contact Person for an Activity from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load.

In the event that the activity is cancelled or your child is unable to attend an activity, you may be eligible for a refund. View the refund policy here. Select Event Refund Policy from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Event Refund Policy from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. View the policy details The key points of the refund policy will load automatically. For more details, you can click View policy details. This will give more details on the policy, and you can access the Request for Refund form.

Use this space to check which activities your children are already registered to participate in. Select Registered Activities from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select Registered Activities from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load.

Use this page to search for upcoming and current activities your child is enrolled in or interested in enrolling in. Select View Activities from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View Activities from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load.

Use this page to search for upcoming camps that you have already consented to your child attending or participating in. Select View consented camps from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View consented camps from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The app will notify you of any consented camps (if any). Note: The app will ask if you want to view withdrawn activities, consented excursions or any events with RSVPs.

Use this page to search for upcoming excursions that you have already consented to your child attending. Select View consented excursions from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View consented excursions from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The app will notify you of any consented excursions (if any). Note: The app will ask if you want to view withdrawn activities, consented camps or any events with RSVPs.

Use this page to search for upcoming and current activities your child is enrolled in. Select View Event from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View Event from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The activities page will automatically load.

Use this page to search for upcoming excursions or events that require an RSVP. Select View events with RSVPs from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View events with RSVPs from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The app will notify you of any events with RSVPs (if any). Note: The app will ask if you want to view withdrawn activities or consented excursions or camps.

Use this page to search for activities or events that have been withdrawn or cancelled. Select View withdrawn activities from the suggested prompts Click Events and Activities from the home screen tiles. Select View withdrawn activities from the suggested prompts. Choose the child whose events you want to see. The app will notify you of any activities that have been withdrawn (if any). Note: The app will then ask whether you want to see consented excursions or camps, as well as any events with RSVPs.

In some cases, you may be eligible for a discount if you settle payment early. Note: You must clear all outstanding fees to be eligible for an early payment discount. Select the Fees tile Tap the Fees tile on the home screen. Select Early payment discount. Read the instructions and eligibility guidelines for the early payment discount.

The app connects to the school's finance system. You can view invoices with fees due to the school. Select Fee Due from the Fees screen Click the Fees tile on the home screen. Select the Fee Due prompt. The app will load your invoices from the school for the current academic year.

The fee schedule outlines the dates for paying school fees per term. Select Fees Schedule from the list of prompts Click the Fees tile from the home screen. Then select the Fees Schedule (current academic year) from the list of Nova prompts. The fee payment schedule will load automatically.

Click the Fees tile on the home screen Select the Fees tile. Nova will provide a selection of prompts to choose from. Select the Pay Outstanding Fees prompt on the screen. Choose your child from the dropdown menu Where there are more than one child enrolled in the school, you can choose the child you would like to make payment for. The payments are listed below each child. Toggle between each child to get the total amount due. Select the outstanding payment You can select more than one payment to make, you can also make payment for all your children. Select all the payments you wish to cover. Make payment You can view the details of each payment by selecting Details and partial payment or tap Make payment. The payment summary will appear where you have the option to either Edit amounts or Proceed to payment. Where the app will connect to the school's finance system to complete the payment.

When siblings are actively enrolled in the same school, you may be eligible for a discount. Select Sibling Discount from the Nova prompts Click the Fees tile on the home screen. Select Sibling Discount from the suggested prompts. Choose the relevant child to check for discount eligibility Select your child from the list to see which discounts are available. The information will automatically appear.

The app provides information on the payment methods the school accepts. Select the Fees tile Select the Fees tile on the home screen. Then select Supported payment methods from the tabs. The information will display automatically. The information includes a note on the school office hours for in-person payments.

Select View Outstanding Fees from the prompt Click the Fees tile on the home screen. Select View Outstanding Fees from the suggested prompts. Select the child to view outstanding fees Choose your child from the dropdown menu. You can total up the fees for one or more children enrolled in the school. Select the fees in question. Click the credit card icon in the top-right corner of the screen. View the fee breakdown The outstanding fees will automatically display in a table by child and amount due. You can pay the outstanding fees at this point. Below the table, you can either Edit amounts or Proceed to payment.

This feature lets you view the account statement for each child enrolled in the school. Select View Statement of Account Click the Fees tile from the home screen. Select the View Statement of Account prompt. Select the child whose statement you want to see A list of every child enrolled in the school will appear. Select the child to view their statement. You will be asked to choose the statement's start and end dates.

Use this feature to view the fees for the upcoming academic year. Select View Upcoming Tuition Fees Select the Fees tile from the home screen. Select View Upcoming Tuition Fees from the prompts. The fees will automatically display.

Click on the Notifications Bell icon On the right side of the navigation bar, tap the bell icon. Select your child's name In cases where more than one child is enrolled in the school, you can choose which notifications you view. Each child's name appears across the top of the screen. Choose between Messages, Alerts or Favourites You can select the Messages, Alerts, or Favourites tabs to view. Click the filter icon in the navigation bar to filter Notifications, as All, Unread, or Read. On the right, a circled checkmark lets you mark all notifications as read.

Open the hamburger menu At the top left of any screen in the app on the navigation bar, tap the hamburger menu (≡). Click Log out At the bottom of the menu, you will find the Log out button. Click it. Note: A pop-up will appear asking you to confirm that you want to log out.
documents.s: Log out of Parent Experience Place (PXP)

documents.t: Home screen and Subject tiles After signing in, the home screen will appear. Here you will see the Navigation bar and the Action Tiles. Click a tile to perform a related task. Use the Navigation Bar The navigation bar runs across the top of the app at all times. A hamburger menu (≡) is on the left; here you can view Notifications, Topics, Settings, and GEMS Rewards.
